rule_citation: PU Code 2827 and 2827.1; Electric Rule 21 (each IOU keeps its own version; R.17-07-007, successor rulemaking R.25-08-004 opened 2025-08-20); NBT: D.22-12-056 (R.20-08-020) as implemented by Res. E-5301, modified by D.23-11-068 and D.24-09-051; NEM 2.0: D.16-01-044; 20-yr NEM legacy: D.14-03-041; NEM-paired storage: D.14-05-033, D.16-04-020, D.18-02-008, D.19-01-030, D.20-06-017; SGIP-to-NBT transition: D.24-03-071
applies_to: IOU only - PG&E, SCE, SDG&E (large IOUs). The small CPUC-jurisdictional IOUs (Bear Valley, Liberty, PacifiCorp) have separately approved NEM/NBT tariffs and their own Rule 21 versions; PacifiCorp uses its OATT process instead of Rule 21 (D.07-07-027). Publicly-owned utilities (LADWP, SMUD, IID, MID, TID and the municipal utilities) are NOT bound by Rule 21 or the NBT and set their own interconnection and export rules - see the utility file. CCA customers inside IOU territory interconnect under the IOU's Rule 21 and NBT; the CCA sets the generation portion of the export credit. Rule 21 does not cover facilities selling into FERC wholesale markets (those use the IOU WDT or the CAISO tariff).
nem_successor: Net Billing Tariff (NBT), marketed by the IOUs as the 'Solar Billing Plan', adopted by D.22-12-056 (2022-12-15). Applies to interconnection applications submitted on or after 2023-04-15. Exports are credited at hourly Energy Export Credit (EEC) prices derived from the CPUC Avoided Cost Calculator (ACC). Customers must take a specific electrification TOU rate: PG&E E-ELEC, SCE TOU-D-PRIME, SDG&E EV-TOU-5 (non-residential customers may use any TOU rate). The NBT legacy period is 9 years from original PTO, for the original customer only; customers who migrate from NEM get no NBT legacy period. Legacy NEM 1.0/2.0 customers keep NEM for 20 years from original PTO (D.14-03-041 / D.16-01-044); the right transfers with the system at the same location. Switching to NBT voluntarily permanently forfeits the remaining NEM term. NEM 2.0 applications submitted by 2023-04-14 had until 2026-04-14 to finish (Secondary - installer guidance).
nem_cap_res_kw: No kW cap - sized-to-load only (SCE Sched. NBT SC 1.b.iii.B: 'there is no limit on the capacity' other than the sized-to-load rule). 1 MW (AC) is the cost-responsibility boundary: above 1 MW, NBT/NEM facilities pay non-NEM fees, study costs and upgrade costs (Rule 21 D.13.a). Capacity uses the lesser of inverter nameplate and CEC-AC rating (AC).
nem_cap_nonres_kw: No kW cap - sized-to-load only; same 1 MW AC cost-responsibility boundary (Rule 21 D.13.a). NEM facilities interconnecting at transmission level are limited to 1 MW or less (D.22-07-001).
nem_aggregate_cap: None for NEM 2.0 or NBT. NEM 1.0 closed when it reached its statutory program cap (calculation clarified in D.12-05-036), which triggered NEM 2.0.
nem_sizing_rule: NBT: estimated output <=100% of prior 12-month usage (kWh), or up to 150% if the customer attests to expected load growth within 12 months. Net surplus is paid at NSC. NEM 2.0: <= the customer's annual onsite load. Expanding a system by more than the greater of 10% or 1 kW of original generating nameplate triggers the NEM/NBT modification rules.
export_credit_value: Hourly ACC-derived EEC prices: 24 hours x weekday/weekend x month (576 values per vintage year), with separate Generation and Delivery components. Prices are locked for 9 years for PTO dates 2023-04-15 through 2027-12-31; later PTO dates float annually. Residential ACC Plus adder (SCE Sched. NBT Rates 3.b, $/kWh by PTO vintage, non-equity/equity): 2023 0.040/0.093; 2024 0.032/0.074; 2025 0.024/0.056; 2026 0.016/0.037; 2027 0.008/0.019; 2028+ 0. Non-residential gets no adder. SDG&E residential customers get no adder. Customers adding solar required by building code (new construction) get no adder. NEM customers who move to NBT get no adder. Values in cents: 2026-vintage SCE adder = 1.6 c/kWh (3.7 c/kWh equity). PG&E adder table not independently read. Net Surplus Compensation at true-up = DLAP 7am-5pm 12-month rolling average (CPUC: roughly 2-3 c/kWh).
credit_rollover: Monthly EEC credits offset energy charges only (not NBCs, minimum charge, demand or fixed charges) and roll forward within the 12-month Relevant Period. At true-up, unused EEC is forfeited and remaining net surplus kWh is paid at NSC. The ACC Plus adder can offset any charge and carries forward until used.
annual_true_up: At the end of the customer's 12-month Relevant Period (anniversary of PTO, or one-time election to move it). NBT bills are paid monthly; NEM 1.0/2.0 settles charges annually. Net surplus is paid at the NSC rate (D.11-06-016).
ic_standard: IEEE 1547-2018 + UL 1741-SB (Rule 21 Sec. D.5 and Secs. Hh/P, smart-inverter requirements under Res. E-5000/E-5036). Inverters must be on the CEC grid-support inverter list. Earlier installs are UL 1741-SA (Phase 1-3 smart inverter).
ic_fast_track_kw: No size limit for NBT/NEM or Non-Export facilities: Rule 21 E.2.b.i says NBT, NEM-1, NEM-2 and all Non-Exporting Generating Facilities are evaluated under Fast Track (Initial Review Screens A-M, Supplemental Review Screens N-P). Other exporting facilities have a voltage-based size table in E.2.b.i that was NOT read (truncated fetch). Secondary source: about 3 MW on 12 kV or higher in PG&E.
ic_simplified_kw: 11 kVA - Screen J ('Is the Gross Rating of the Generating Facility 11 kVA or less?'). Screen K: NEM facility <=500 kW. Secondary source: ICA Screen M is not applied at <=30 kVA.
ic_application_fee: NBT/NEM <=1 MW: one-time fee set per IOU from historical costs - PG&E $145, SCE $94, SDG&E $132 (CPUC NEM/NBT page). These facilities are also exempt from Supplemental Review fees, study costs and distribution/network upgrade costs, and paired storage keeps the exemption if total nameplate is <=1 MW. Non-NEM, non-export and >1 MW requests: $800 Interconnection Request fee (Rule 21 Table E.1) plus study costs. Optional pre-application report: $300; enhanced reports $225, $800 or $1,025.
ic_study_trigger_kw: 1000 - above 1 MW the Rule 21 D.13 NBT/NEM exemptions end, and the customer pays study and upgrade costs and follows non-NEM timelines. At any size, failing Initial Review screens (e.g. Screen M ICA/15% of peak load) moves the project to Supplemental Review, then Independent Study or Distribution Group Study.
external_disconnect: Utility discretion - Rule 21 Sec. H.1.d / Hh.1.d 'Visible Disconnect Required'. Secondary source: PG&E does not require a separate AC disconnect where the service has a single-phase self-contained revenue meter. The local AHJ may still require one.
insurance_required: Unclear - no Rule 21 insurance requirement for NBT/NEM facilities was found in the portion of Rule 21 read (the tariff fetch was truncated before the insurance provisions).
ic_timeline_days: NBT/NEM <=1 MW: PTO normally within 30 business days after receipt of a complete request, a signed agreement and final electrical inspection (Rule 21 D.13.b). Pre-application report: 10 business days. Secondary source: NGOM install 40 business days; distribution upgrades 120 business days (D.20-09-035). Non-Export Energy Storage may elect the expedited process in Rule 21 Sec. N (D.14).
non_export_option: Yes - well defined. Rule 21 Screen I (G.1.i) non-export and limited-export options: reverse-power or minimum-power relays; certified Power Control Systems (PCS) with open-loop response time of 2 s or less can use Fast Track (Secondary: Energy Toolbase summary of the Res. E-5000-era changes). Other paths: Sec. M / Mm inadvertent export using UL 1741 SA-listed inverters; Sec. N expedited interconnection for Non-Export Energy Storage; Sec. O certified non-export AC/DC converters; Rule 21 Non-Export agreement. NEM/NBT expansions above the 10%/1 kW limit can go on a Non-Export agreement without losing legacy status. Limited Generation Profiles (Res. E-5230 workshops) are an emerging path.
storage_counts_toward_cap: No for the sized-to-load test, which uses renewable generator output only. Yes for the 1 MW threshold: Integrated or Directly Connected storage nameplate is added to aggregate facility nameplate (SCE Sched. NBT SC 1.b.iii.B). Large paired storage (>10 kW AC) is capped at 150% of the renewable generator's maximum output (D.19-01-030). D.20-06-017 suspended that cap from 2020-08-16; an Executive Director extension ran it to 2025-08-15. Whether the 150% cap is now enforced again is Unclear. Small paired storage (<=10 kW) has no relative size limit. SCE Sched. NBT SC 5.a.ii (Sheet 27, Advice 5228-E) says the waiver was extended by the Executive Director on 2023-09-05 and the 150% limit 'shall not apply until on and after August 16, 2025' - read literally the cap applies again from 2025-08-16; no later extension found, but not confirmed either. No limit on storage kWh.
standby_charge: None for NEM/NBT generation: NEM customers are exempt from standby charges (CPUC NEM page), and SCE Sched. NBT Rates 5 says no Standby or Customer Generation Departing Load charges apply to the NBT generating facility's capacity. Non-eligible generators on the same premises are not exempt.
